text:
When a $6.3bn exploit hits the largest exchange, the usual question is whether the market can absorb it.

Our reading of last week is that the more useful question is how fast the damage was contained.

Approximately $2.8bn of stolen assets were rapidly frozen by Circle, Tether and other issuers. Binance has reportedly replenished affected funds through its own reserves and insurance fund. The exploit represented a small fraction of Binance's $171bn in customer assets.

For allocators, the point is structural. Onchain infrastructure is transparent, so stolen assets can be traced and frozen, and that capability has matured.

The broader read, including where Bitcoin sits against key technical support and how cross-asset conditions are shaping up ahead of the US midterms, is in this week's Weekly.
